title: Writing and Comparing Fractions · Ashley and Ben
subject: Word Problems

match.first: What fraction of the students in the school are in grade 4?

items.prompt: What fraction of the students in the school are in grade 4?

steps.why: Add all four class groups for grade 4. The whole school is 482. The glasses and siblings fractions are not needed here.
The part is the grade 4 students. Add every boy and girl from both classes.
Ms. Ashley has 21 and Mr. Ben has 24, so grade 4 has 45 students.
A fraction is part over whole: 45 grade 4 students out of 482 students.

items.context: There are 482 students in the school and there are two Grade 4 classes: Ms. Ashley’s and Mr. Ben’s classes. Ms. Ashley’s class has 15 boys and 6 girls. Mr. Ben’s class has 14 girls and 10 boys. In Ms. Ashley’s class, 2/3 of the students wear glasses. In Mr. Ben’s class, 1/4 of the kids have other siblings in the school.

items.prompt: What fraction of the grade 4 students are boys?

steps.why: Boys are in both classes, so use both boy numbers. The whole is all 45 grade 4 students.
The part is all the boys. The whole is grade 4 only, not the whole school.
There are 25 boys out of 45 students.
Divide the top and bottom by 5 to simplify. Answer: 25/45, or 5/9.

items.prompt: What fraction of the grade 4 students are in Ms. Ashley’s class?

steps.why: Only Ms. Ashley’s class counts for the part. The whole is all 45 grade 4 students.
Add the boys and girls in her class. Mr. Ben’s numbers are not part of it.
Ms. Ashley has 21 of the 45 students.
Divide the top and bottom by 3 to simplify. Answer: 21/45, or 7/15.

items.prompt: What fraction of the students in Mr. Ben’s class that do not have siblings in the same school?

steps.why: The story gives the fraction that DO have siblings. The question asks for those who do not.
mark: 1/4 of the kids have other siblings in the school

steps.why: The whole class is 4 out of 4. Take away the part that has siblings.
Subtract the tops: 4 − 1 = 3. The bottom stays 4.
3 out of every 4 students do not have siblings in the school.

items.prompt: In Ms. Ashley’s class, are there more students that wear glasses or do not wear glasses?
items.answer: Since 2/3 of the students wear glasses, only 1/3 students do not wear glasses. So, more students wear glasses.

steps.why: This is the only fraction we need. The question compares glasses to no glasses.
The whole class is 3 out of 3. Subtract the part that wears glasses.
The bottoms are the same, so the bigger top is the bigger fraction. 2 is more than 1.
2/3 is more than 1/3 of the class.

items.prompt: There are 1/35 of the students in the school that are allergic to seafood. There are 1/15 of the students in the school that are allergic to peanuts. Are there more students allergic to seafood or peanuts?
items.answer: Since 1/35 < 1/15, more students are allergic to peanuts.

steps.why: These two fractions are the ones to compare. Both are parts of the whole school.
Find a number that both 35 and 15 go into. 105 works: 35 × 3 and 15 × 7.
Multiply the top and bottom of each fraction by the same number.
3 is less than 7, so more students are allergic to peanuts.
